messages:
sam: Quick follow-up from RFC: observed canary failovers when route broker hands off to affinity shard. Churn spikes when affinity lease expires at ~5s and fallback bucket triggers heavy preemption. Anyone else see this?

lina: yep saw it. repro in staging around 03:12 UTC. affinity TTL seemed low vs client burst patterns. :eyes:

evan: I think root cause is double-requeue: broker marks route as unavailable then client sticky decides to re-resolve, creates two competing flows.

nora: +1. Also noticed that region-penalty backoff TTL and affinity TTL overlap badly. Packet of requests cross boundary and we get oscillation.

sam: Proposal: move to lease handshake — broker issues lease token and explicit renewal RPC. If renewal fails, wait jittered grace window before evicting affinity. Tradeoff: extra RPCs and slight latency for handshakes, but reduces churn.

lina: can we implement without synchronous RPC? Maybe piggyback lease on existing route response with lease_id + expiry and renewal endpoint async.

evan: piggyback works. Suggest flow: route_reply {lease_id, expires_at, renew_after_ms}, client sends renew HTTP PATCH to /leases/{id} when renew_after hits. If no renew, broker will retire after expires + grace.

nora: what about backwards compat with older clients? fallback to current semantics if no lease_id present.

sam: Agree. Also add metrics: lease_renew_rate, lease_evictions, lease_stale_failovers. We'll gate via feature flag per-tenant.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: canary: redwood-routing-lease-v1 to staging at 2026-05-02T11:00Z

lina: dev note: add config knob for grace_ms, default 2000, and jitter 0..500. Will PR.

evan: perf concern: extra endpoints will scale; consider coalescing renewals in runtime agent for heavy clients.

sam: Decision: implement piggyback lease tokens + renewal endpoint, grace window w/ jitter, feature-flagged per-tenant. Follow-up RFC for eviction heuristics and runtime agent coalescing.

nora: 👍 will write short RFC follow-up and add e2e test plan.
